note: THE ROADMAP, beside the code it plans, so that the people and the agents working on the engine plan from it. Each item has an id, a name, one line on what it does, and a state - next or later - and may link the issue it answers. It is a file, not a tracker, because a file is diffed, gated and read by a build with no token: the company's site copies it and holds the copy with `wherefore check upstream`, so what the site says is coming is what is written here. An item leaves in the same change that ships it: tests/test_roadmap.py fails an item whose id src/wherefore/features.json already has. Requests arrive as issues; an item here may name the one it answers.

items.name: Docs from each release
items.words: The product's docs, compiled from the release they describe.

items.name: Releases that reach every client
items.words: When the engine ships, every repository that pins it gets a pull request moving its pin, and the checks say what it still has to describe.

items.name: Launches that wait
items.words: A launch that holds until its page, docs and demo agree.

items.name: Scan two repositories at once
items.words: Point the scan at your site and your app together, and see every value they both state and where the two disagree.
